notes.claim: On discharge, sulphuric acid leaves the electrolyte and binds to the plate as lead sulphate, so the liquid becomes lighter and its specific gravity falls; on charge the acid concentration rises.
For an accurate voltage reading the battery needs to rest open circuit for at least four hours; makers recommend 24 hours for lead acid.
A cell voltage of 2.10 V at room temperature indicates about 90 per cent charge.
Surface charge shows an elevated voltage straight after charging, and a brief discharge before measuring counteracts the error.
Colder electrolyte reads a higher specific gravity, so readings are corrected; one maker adds one point (0.001) per 3 degrees F above 77 degrees F, and subtracts below it.
Evaporation of water raises the specific gravity reading and overfilling lowers it, so electrolyte level matters when reading it.
Acid concentrated at the bottom of a cell makes the battery appear more charged than it is and raises the open circuit voltage artificially.

A cell's open-circuit voltage is roughly its specific gravity plus 0.845 V, so a stationary cell full at 1.225 rests near 2.07 V, lower than a cell with stronger acid (added for i2's voltmeter model).
